widget.instructions: Drag the intercept a with its slider: the line x/a + y/a = 1 cuts both axes at a. Make it pass through P.

args.text: Substitute P into your equation: does it hold?

stem: A line passes through P({{px}}, {{py}}) and cuts off equal, non-zero intercepts on the two axes.

hints.text: Intercept form: x/a + y/b = 1. Equal intercepts mean a = b.
So the line is x/a + y/a = 1, i.e. x + y = a. Substitute P to find a.

intercepts-opposite-sign.text: Equal intercepts means the same signed value on both axes, so the line is x + y = a, slope −1. Your line has slope +1 (intercepts of opposite sign).

point-as-intercepts.text: P's coordinates aren't the intercepts. The intercepts are equal (a and a) and P lies on the line.

generic.text: Write x + y = a and make P satisfy it.

workedSolution.text: Equal intercepts a: x/a + y/a = 1, so x + y = a.
P lies on it: a = {{px}} + ({{py}}) = {{s}}. The line is x + y = {{s}}.

intercepts-opposite-sign.front: A line with equal intercepts a on both axes?

point-as-intercepts.front: Is a point on a line the same as its intercepts?
point-as-intercepts.back: No: intercepts are where the line cuts the axes.

accessibility.altText: The point P({{px}}, {{py}}) and a trial line with equal intercepts a.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use the a slider or its arrow keys; type your answer in the box.
